card.title: Reading across genres — one spine, four lenses

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Seven stories (Winton's Neighbours on migration unease, Desai's Devoted Son on filial duty curdling, Márquez's winged old man as magical-realist patience-test), five poems (Dickinson's slant Day, Thomas's waking prayer, de Burgos's self-route feminism), five essays (Sacks on libraries, Russell on knowledge vs wisdom, Harari on humility) and three one-act plays (Molnár's husbands, Strindberg's death, Tiwari's Bull). One spine answers all: claim → quoted moment → technique → purpose.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: every answer: theme-claim → textual moment (quote) → technique (irony/symbol/dialogue/image) → author purpose  ·  stories: character + turning point · poems: speaker + image + device · essays: thesis + argument moves · plays: conflict + stage moment

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Claims need quoted moments — unquoted readings score thin. Genre lenses differ (magical realism read literally collapses; satire read straight inverts meaning). Separate narrator from author (Desai ≠ her son; Thapa's Buddha-eyes narrator frames, not preaches).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Márquez demands symbolic patience (the wings resist single meaning — that IS the point). Russell's knowledge/wisdom split structures whole essays. One-act plays compress to a single crisis — answer from the climax backward. de Burgos and Okri reward postcolonial framing; Sacks rewards humanist detail.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Sample spine on Neighbours: claim — migration unease dissolves through observed ritual; moment — the newcomers' garden slowly mirroring the street's rhythms (quote the turning passage); technique — Winton's patient accumulation of domestic detail; purpose — belonging as practice, not status. Four moves, any text.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Theme-hunting flattens texts into morals — detail first, slogan never. One framework cannot serve satire and elegy identically; adjust per genre. Author intention is partly unknowable — argue from the page, not biography.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From text outward: collect striking moments → cluster into theme → name each moment's technique (irony, image, dialogue, structure) → state the effect on the reader as purpose. The method is genre-parametric: swap the technique vocabulary (prosody for poems, stagecraft for plays) and the engine runs unchanged.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Titles are theses; endings reveal purpose — read backward from the close. One exact short quote beats paraphrase paragraphs. Device + effect, never device alone. Keep a two-line dossier per text (theme + killer quote) for revision week.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: theme-with-moments on any story/essay; device + effect on poems; character analysis via turning points; one-act conflict + stage significance; comparative theme pairs.
